sentences.text: Well-preserved full body fossils show that Paracestracion differed from living bullhead sharks by having a shorter skull and different placements for the pelvic girdle and fins.

The genus includes up to six species, including P. bellis from England, the type species P. falcifer from England and Germany, P. sarstedtensis and P. viohli from Germany, and an indeterminate species from Luxembourg.
The species P. pectinatus from the Early Cretaceous of France is known only from isolated teeth.
The genus Paracestracion was first described in 1911 by Ernst Hermann Friedrich von Koken in Karl Alfred von Zittel.
Recent studies have classified Paracestracion into its own family, Paracestracionidae.
The parent group of Paracestracion is the family Heterodontidae.
Paracestracion lived from the Early Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous in rocks found in England, France, Germany, and Luxembourg.
Paracestracion lived between 184.2 and 132.6 million years ago, from the Toarcian to the Valanginian stages.
